summary: Dispatched the tick-period sweep the placeholder-shift question needed. The retained evidence for the shift sat only at a 1000 ms tick period (the fixed experiment and its repeat), while the 80 ms observation that returned the correct index was construction feedback rather than a receipt — so the condition that the queued placeholders must survive the flush-to-truncation window was not receipt-backed at more than one tick period. I parameterised the case into `run_shift_case(mode, tick_ms)` with every sleep derived from the tick period and added three sweep points (100, 250, 500 ms) beside the existing 1000 ms reference, each with its own admission, mode-specific result event and comparison; the harness change makes this a revision of the same fixed experiment whose earlier revision and both receipts stay in the record. Locally the 500 ms point already violates the obligation — `resolved` ok with `assigned_idx` 3 while entry 33 is at index 1 and the decided log is 33,34,35 — so I expect that point to be violated and flagged the two lower points as the ones that would narrow the condition if they return the correct index. Incomplete: the sweep receipt is pending; the exact threshold between 250 and 500 ms, and any tick period below 100 ms, remain outside this probe's reach.
